checks.claim: The average new car weighs a bit over 4,000 pounds, about 4,300 or more by recent EPA data (4,354 lb per the EPA's 2025 Automotive Trends Report).
checks.why: About 4,000 lb was accurate around 2018-2022, but the newest EPA-based figure is about 4,354 lb, so the claim as written is dated.

sources.title: Here's How Much The Average Car Weighs These Days, And Why It Matters - Jalopnik
Are New Cars and Trucks Getting Heavier?

checks.claim: A bag with an effective diameter of about six inches, at 100 psi, supports roughly 2,800 pounds. Real bags give a bit less, depending on their shape and height.
checks.why: Force = pressure x effective area; a 6-inch circle at 100 psi gives about 2,827 lb. Real bags use effective area, which varies with height, and rated loads are lower (e.g. a 6.60 in max diameter spring is rated 1,600 lb).

checks.claim: Bags usually top out around 100 psi, and the tank is typically filled to about 150-200 psi.
checks.why: 100 psi is the typical maximum for bags, not the everyday setting. Tank and compressor ratings in kits run 150, 175 and 200 psi, so 'up to about 150' is on the low side. The tank figures come from retailer pages.

checks.claim: About three-quarters of new semi trailers use air suspension, and it's widely used on buses and ambulances.
checks.why: FAMA supports about 75% of new trailers. There is no hard figure for city buses ('most' unverified) and no share for ambulances, so 'many' is unquantified; use softer wording.
